newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate drops to 7.7 from 9.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate drops to 7.7 from 9.2 pct.

text.p: The Croatian lending rate dropped to 7.7 percent on Friday from 9.2 percent after all lenders lowered their short-term rates, despite a rise in kuna demand.
Call money fell to 7.7 from 12 percent on fresh placements of 16 million kuna.
Insurers rolled over previous five-10 and 10-15 day loans at a new lower rate of seven percent, down from eight percent.
Only the 31-366 day rate was up, to 11.5 from 9.9 percent.
Total settlements rose to 38.9 million kuna but were still largely overshot by supply.
Overnight trade on Thursday was down to 20.8 million kuna thanks to lower shortfalls at two commercial bank borrowers.

The central bank calculated the kuna midrates for Saturday and next Monday slightly weaker at 5.2553 to the dollar but firmer at 3.5511 from 3.5547 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
